text:
Troy Stecher scored with 28 seconds left in regulation to give Toronto a 5-4 win over the Rangers and push the Maple Leafs' winning streak to three games. Stecher's wrist shot, set up by Morgan Rielly and Brandon Duhaime, came just under five minutes after Alexis Lafrenière tied the game for New York with his own wrist shot. Both late goals came on chances of about 3 percent, which tells you how little either side had to work with in the closing minutes.

The Leafs' win was no fluke. Expected goals, a measure of the quality of each team's chances, favored Toronto 2.98 to 1.98, and the Leafs outshot New York 35 to 25. By the deserved-to-win measure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, Toronto took 68 percent of them. The second period was the clearest gap, 1.60 expected goals to 1.08, even as the teams traded the lead twice. Duhaime, who scored once and assisted twice, had Toronto out-chancing New York 0.68 to 0.18 while he was on the ice. For the Rangers, Adam Fox had four assists and was on the ice for 1.40 expected goals for against 0.78 against. The Rangers hit more (34 to 19), but Toronto blocked 16 shots to their 6.

Both goalies finished 2.02 goals worse than their shots deserved, a stat called goals saved above expected. Sergei Bobrovsky and Dylan Garand each let in more than the chances warranted, which helps explain a game with nine goals. The Leafs leave with three wins in a row. The Rangers leave with a one-goal loss and no points.
